item.title: NPR: Trump's arch is on the verge of federal approval. But a judge could block construction
item.description: A federal panel will meet to consider the arch for final approval on Thursday, and the government said it may begin construction later that same day. Critics hope a judge will intervene last-minute.

item.title: NPR: The South flexes political power in midterms, sets regional influence in 2028 election
item.description: Tuesday's dramatic midterm results have transformed the electoral map, ensuring the path to future power for Democrats and Republicans must run through the South and its diverse voting population.

item.title: NPR: Democrats will control Congress. Will it change Trump's approach to foreign policy?
item.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with historian and journalist Anne Applebaum about how much a Democrat-led Congress can steer foreign policy.

item.title: NPR: Morning news brief
item.description: Democrats are planning out how to tackle their agenda in the new year, ballots are still being counted in some undecided races, Trump avoids taking the blame after GOP midterm losses.

item.title: NPR: Democrats will take control of Congress next year. What does it mean for the economy?
item.description: The Democratic gains in this week's midterm elections will bring a different business climate to Washington. But the overall economy should be OK.

item.title: NPR: Democrats and Republicans reflect on midterm results and the message sent by voters
item.description: The 2026 election proved to be very good for Democrats and very bad for President Trump and Republicans. But there are still races outstanding that can tell us what mattered to voters this year.

item.title: NPR: Trump blames GOP candidates and Fox News for midterm losses
item.description: President Trump has blamed GOP candidates and Fox News in the wake of the sweeping Democratic sweep during the midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Midterm voters rebuke Trump, handing Democrats both chambers of Congress
item.description: Voters delivered a sweeping rebuke of President Trump and his party in the midterms, handing Democrats major victories and dramatically reshaping the balance of power in Washington. Trump now enters a lame duck phase of his second term, promising both to use his veto power, and also to work across the aisle as he faces the largest Democratic majorities in decades. Liz Landers reports.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Officials in Iran welcome midterm results as vote against war
item.description: In our news wrap Wednesday, top officials in Iran welcomed the results of the U.S. midterm elections, Israeli President Isaac Herzog says he's accepted the results of last week's election and will consult with party leaders on forming a new government and Ukraine's air force says Russia launched more than 300 drones overnight.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Breaking down the Democrats' big majorities after the blue wave
item.description: The results of the midterms have set up a two-year power struggle between Trump's White House and the incoming Democratic Congress. Lisa Desjardins takes a look at the races and the potential size of the incoming Democratic majority.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The issues that drove voters' decisions in the midterms
item.description: For a deeper dive into the election data and why people voted the way they did, Geoff Bennett and Amna Nawaz spoke with Amy Walter of The Cook Political Report.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A NASA space telescope plunged back to Earth after a mission that lasted 11 times longer than planned
item.description: The Swift Observatory's demise came less than three months after a long-shot rescue mission failed.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'A mandate for change': Progressive Democrat William Lawrence flips House seat in Michigan
item.description: In Michigan's 7th Congressional District, progressive activist William Lawrence unseated Republican Tom Barrett in one of the year's most competitive House races. Lawrence joined Amna Nawaz to discuss the win and what comes next.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New Mexico's Deb Haaland on making history as first Native American woman elected governor
item.description: The election led to several historic firsts. In New Hampshire, Chris Pappas became the first openly gay man to be elected to the Senate. In Georgia, Keisha Lance Bottoms will be the first Black woman governor. And in New Mexico, Deb Haaland will make history as the first Native American woman to serve as a governor. Haaland joined Geoff Bennett to discuss more.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: OKC's Republican mayor says election wipeout is 'rejection of Trumpism'
item.description: President Trump has sought to deflect blame for the sweeping Republican losses. But within the party, some are beginning to ask whether they have been too deferential to the president — and whether the GOP needs to rethink its identity. Amna Nawaz discussed what comes next with David Holt, the Republican mayor of Oklahoma City.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How the Latino shift to Democrats helped turn Texas blue
item.description: A major factor in the midterm elections was the number of Latino voters who headed to the polls and supported Democrats. For perspective on this massive swing, Amna Nawaz spoke with María Teresa Kumar, CEO of Voto Latino, an organization that helps register Hispanic and Latino voters.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democratic and GOP strategists on how parties should respond to midterm results
item.description: For perspective on how both parties are responding to the historic election wins, Geoff Bennett spoke with two strategists from both sides of the political aisle. Mo Elleithee is the former spokesman for the Democratic National Committee, and Doug Heye is a former spokesman for the Republican National Committee.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope Leo XIV welcomes Bob Dylan to the Vatican in a brief visit
item.description: Leo gave Dylan a rosary, while Dylan presented the pope with a copy of his autobiography, "Chronicles: Volume One."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Shorter days and dark afternoons can trigger depression. Here's how to fight back
item.description: As winter approaches and daylight hours grow shorter, people prone to seasonal depression can feel it in their bodies and brains.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ex-Prince Andrew called to testify in civil case, 1st royal in 156 years to get witness summons
item.description: The former Prince Andrew has been called to testify as a witness in a civil fraud trial, marking what is believed to be the first time in more than 150 years that a member of the royal family has received a witness summons, British media reported on Wednesday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What's next in the investigation of the Learjet crash in Florida that killed 9?
item.description: Investigators are just beginning the lengthy process of determining why a business jet plummeted from the sky in Florida after encountering a thunderstorm and slammed into the ground with such force that it created a crater and shattered the plane.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Florida sheriff says 2 dead, including suspect, as witnesses report shooting at Tampa office complex
item.description: Florida authorities said two people were dead, including a suspect, after witnesses reported a shooting Wednesday at Citibank's sprawling business complex that employs thousands in the Tampa area.

item.title: NPR: What's the future of the Democratic party in Texas, amid historic midterm wins?
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with former Texas state Sen. Wendy Davis, a Democrat, about Texas flipping blue and what it means for future elections.

item.title: NPR: South Carolina winner Annie Andrews talks about her win and the path ahead
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with Democrat Dr. Annie Andrews, who bested Republican candidate Darline Graham, the incumbent and sister of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Democrats win full control of more state governments and the Texas House
item.description: Democrats in Texas took control of the state House after historic wins for governor and U.S. Senate, part of a series of sweeping gains nationwide in Tuesday's elections that shifted the balance of power across several battleground and Republican-leaning states.

item.title: NPR: Where voters stand on state ballot measures, from abortion to LGBTQ rights to guns
item.description: Voters in dozens of states considered 146 statewide ballot measures this midterm cycle, on topics spanning LGBTQ rights, wealth taxes, abortion, redistricting, guns and more.

item.title: NPR: Rahm Emanuel maps out a vision for what Democrats can achieve after taking Congress
item.description: NPR's Ailsa Chang talks with former congressman and Obama advisor Rahm Emanuel about what Democrats' strategy should be, now that they'll soon control both houses of Congress.

item.title: NPR: Democrats sweeping victories mean big changes for Trump's final two years in office
item.description: Democrats' wins in the House and Senate mean a new power dynamic is coming to Washington.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Israel's president takes first steps on building new government after accepting election results
item.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Wednesday accepted the certified results of last week's parliamentary elections as legally binding and began consultations with party representatives on forming a new government.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: U.S. stocks surge, and the Dow soars 1,500 points as Brent oil's price drops below $95 per barrel
item.description: U.S. stocks are soaring Wednesday after President Donald Trump's party lost its sole control of Washington in the midterm elections.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump-backed redistricting sought a midterm edge for Republicans. It didn't work
item.description: Republicans lost most of the Democratic-held seats they had targeted to flip, lost others they had banked on retaining and got swept out of power by a Democratic surge fueled by voter dissatisfaction with Trump, the economy and the war with Iran.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump previews ballroom construction the day after voters rejected GOP rule
item.description: President Donald Trump gave extended comments Wednesday, not about the Republican Party's midterm election wipeout but instead justifying his building a sprawling White House ballroom.

item.title: NPR: Disney, ABC battle Trump's FCC in court over free speech protections
item.description: President Trump has repeatedly called for Disney's ABC to fire late night comedian Jimmy Kimmel, for mocking him. Trump has also routinely denounced ABC's The View , accusing it of being unfair.

item.title: NPR: FBI's spy hunting squads hit with deep cuts even as foreign espionage threats soar
item.description: The cuts come as a consequence of President Trump and FBI Director Kash Patel's focus on violent crime and immigration, leaving other priorities understaffed.

item.title: NPR: Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey's new Pentagon roles raise ethics worries
item.description: Musk's company, SpaceX, and Luckey's company Anduril, could potentially benefit from recommendations made in the study about future autonomous weapon systems.

item.title: NPR: Democrats' advantage is clear with less than a month to go in the midterm elections
item.description: President Trump is facing low approval ratings, and voters are blaming him for rising costs. Republicans are likely to pay the price at the ballot box next month.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Helpful or harmful? When it comes to AI and young kids, experts have these tips for parents
item.description: By the time that a child is preschool age, they have the ability to learn information from technology, said Lauren Girouard, a researcher at Harvard Graduate School of Education and the University of Michigan.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about Spain's housing protests sparked by an 87-year-old woman's eviction
item.description: Public outrage over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman has put Spain's progressive government under immense pressure to tackle the nation's entrenched housing cost crisis.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: No arrests after Georgia block party shooting as police pursue who killed 2 and injured dozens
item.description: Whoever opened fire at a sprawling block party in rural southern Georgia over the weekend, killing two people and leaving nearly three dozen others injured, remained at large Monday as authorities offered no new information about the shootings.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court hears case on holding energy companies liable for climate change
item.description: Supreme Court justices heard arguments in a major climate change case that could shape how communities hold industries accountable. Officials in Boulder, Colorado, are seeking compensation from energy companies for the costs of natural disasters they say are caused by climate change. Ali Rogin discussed more with News Hour Supreme Court analyst and SCOTUSBlog cofounder Amy Howe.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Tamara Keith and Amy Walter on Trump's payout promises
item.description: NPR's Tamara Keith and Amy Walter of the Cook Political Report with Amy Walter join Geoff Bennett to discuss the latest political news, including President Trump continuing to promise payouts to voters if Republicans win in the midterms, the GOP spending campaign money and playing defense in typically Republican districts and the White House again barring a media outlet from the press pool.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'American Pope' traces Leo's journey from Chicago to the Vatican
item.description: Pope Leo XIV made history as the first American to lead the Catholic Church. But the path that brought him there stretched from Chicago's South Side to decades of missionary work in Peru and ultimately to the highest ranks of the Vatican. "American Pope" traces that journey and offers a fuller portrait of the man behind the papacy. Geoff Bennett spoke with authors Scott Detrow and Daniel Burke.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Cornell students protest handling of alleged rape
item.description: In our news wrap Monday, students at Cornell are staging protests over the university's handling of an alleged fraternity house gang rape in 2024, President Trump said a threat linked to Iran was the reason the U.S. withdrew its bombers from the Fairford airbase in the UK and Dennis Hastert, the disgraced former House Speaker who later went to prison, has died.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about pneumonic plague after Russian lab worker's death
item.description: The U.S. is closely monitoring a potential case of pneumonic plague in Russia after a laboratory worker who studied the disease fell ill and died. Russian authorities insist there is no cause for alarm, but officials have imposed quarantines and other measures at several medical facilities in Siberia. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Annie Jacobsen, author of "Biological War: A Scenario."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Marine's murder charge in Japan fuels local debate over U.S. military presence
item.description: A U.S. Marine has been arrested in Japan on suspicion of robbing and murdering a woman. The Japanese government has lodged a complaint with the U.S. and is demanding full cooperation with the investigation. From Okinawa, special correspondent Patrick Fok explains how the case threatens to revive tensions over America's military presence there, one of the most critical strategic outposts in Asia.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: As GLP-1s reshape America, questions and new uses emerge
item.description: Hailed by some as miracle drugs, GLP-1s have surged in popularity in the past few years. An estimated one out of every eight Americans is now on some version of them and scientists continue to research new potential uses. But with that rapid expansion, there's a growing list of questions and skeptics. William Brangham reports for our new series, GLP-1s: Reshaping America.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about a Russian lab worker's death and speculation about pneumonic plague
item.description: Local officials have confirmed the illness and death of a lab worker at an anti-plague research institute in Russia.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Laotian man deported by U.S. to Eswatini is released after more than a year in prison
item.description: Phone Chomsavanh was among five immigrants deported to Eswatini — where he has no ties — in July 2025 in the early days of the Trump administration's secretive and highly contentious third-country deportation program.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Sen. Tillis says his vote for Hegseth was 'biggest regret of my career' in new book
item.description: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis says in a new book that his deciding vote to confirm Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in January 2025 is the "biggest regret of my career" and that he also "should've stopped" Robert F. Kennedy Jr. from becoming Health and Human Services secretary in the early days of President Donald Trump's second term.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in physics is …
item.description: The Nobel Prize in physics will be announced Tuesday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH: Trump administration issues final rule on transparency in healthcare coverage
item.description: At a news conference, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said the new rule provides a "clear view of what healthcare actually costs."
item.category: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ohio Democrats' path to governor's office runs through rural areas that have turned against party
item.description: Democrats say their nominee for governor in Ohio, Dr. Amy Acton, represents the party's best chance in years to win that office.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Florida's dengue outbreak is largest in continental U.S. in decades
item.description: Experts warn that local dengue outbreaks could become more frequent due to persistent mosquito populations and climate conditions.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Saudi-backed coalition forces Houthis from several areas around key strait, Yemeni officials say
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen says it has recaptured key areas around the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Houthi rebels.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: After redistricting, a Black community in Louisiana faces a future without a champion in Congress
item.description: Scotlandville is a predominantly Black community in Louisiana, that's facing challenges in its political representation. Residents fear losing a representative who understands their struggles.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Lula shake-ups campaign as Flávio Bolsonaro reaches for more support ahead of Brazil's runoff
item.description: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will spend Monday trying to shake-up his campaign after losing the first round of national elections to Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pope Francis' diaries to be published next month, revealing reflections on Vatican years
item.description: The first Latin American pope was known for his humility and outreach to marginalized communities.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Ukraine claims its strikes have taken out more than half of Russia's oil refining capacity
item.description: Ukraine's defense ministry said that recent attacks on refineries, including those in Moscow and Yaroslavl, had disabled 51% of Russia's refining capacity. The claim could not be independently verified.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Obama to campaign with El-Sayed in Detroit as ex-president gets more involved in midterms
item.description: Obama is upping involvement in the midterm election. He taped two dozen ads last week for Democratic candidates for governor and Senate that will be released in the coming days and weeks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Washington Capitals captain Alex Ovechkin says he'll retire at the end of his 22nd season
item.description: Ovechkin has spent his entire career with Washington, winning the Calder Trophy as rookie of the year in 2005-06, the Hart Trophy as MVP three times and leading the NHL in scoring nine times.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Former Prince Andrew files legal action challenging warrants that led to searches of his homes
item.description: If the court rules in his favor, it could prevent authorities from using evidence found during the searches in any prosecution.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court rejects Michigan woman's appeal over school's ban on 'Let's Go Brandon' sweatshirts
item.description: The mother of two boys says their First Amendment rights were violated when they were told to take off the sweatshirts she bought them for Christmas in 2022.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt lands her next gig as Fox News contributor
item.description: Leavitt follows Kayleigh McEnany, the former press secretary who joined Fox in 2021.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Dennis Hastert, longtime Republican House speaker who went to prison, dies at age 84
item.description: Hastert, who was speaker from 1999 until 2007 and spent more than a year in prison later in life, died Saturday of natural causes at his home while receiving hospice care.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A U.S. Marine has been arrested in the killing of a woman on Okinawa, triggering outrage in Japan
item.description: Residents on Okinawa have long been frustrated by the burden of hosting American troops.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court rejects Roy Moore's push to restore $8.2 million defamation verdict awarded to him
item.description: Justices declined to hear Moore's appeal of a lower court decision that vacated the verdict.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump campaigns with Ricketts in Nebraska, where ranchers have beef with his import plan
item.description: The Trump administration's plan to allow more imports of foreign beef has particularly roiled the agriculture-rich state of Nebraska.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A Russian report says a worker at a Siberian plague research institute fell ill and died of an unknown cause
item.description: Although unconfirmed reports suggest pneumonic plague, officials have not publicly identified the infection.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Jeffries says House Democrats aiming to repeat 2018 sweep by flipping Trump districts
item.description: The Democratic Party is working to expand the map by going on offense in Republican-held districts, while President Donald Trump hits the trail in a red-state sprint to boost voter enthusiasm and shore up support from his base.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bolsonaro and Lula head to a runoff in Brazil's presidential election
item.description: Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro, an ally of President Donald Trump, and Brazil's incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will face off in a runoff Oct. 25 for the top job of Latin America's powerhouse economy after neither won a majority in Sunday's vote.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: LISTEN LIVE: Supreme Court hears case seeking damages from fossil fuel industry for climate change
item.description: On Monday, the first day of the Supreme Court's new term, the justices will hear the Boulder case that could decide the fate of others like it.

item.title: NPR: Supreme Court's new term kicks off with blockbuster climate change case
item.description: The case centers on whether local governments can hold giant energy companies accountable for the local harms of climate change, but it has repercussions beyond climate.

item.title: NPR: Voters are increasingly using AI chatbots to fact-check and compare candidates
item.description: Voters are already voting in the midterms. This year, some voters are trying something new to get ready for the election: asking AI to help research their ballot and even decide who to vote for.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP report: U.S. Air Force removes all bombers from British air base targeted by a suspected terror attack
item.description: The U.S. Air Force has brought home its bombers stationed at a U.S.-run military air base in England used to strike Iran following an investigation into a planned terror attack at the RAF Fairford base.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Major oil exporters agree to keep production steady in November
item.description: The so-called OPEC+ subgroup — Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman — will meet again on Nov. 1 to review conditions in the oil market.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in medicine is ...
item.description: The Nobel Prize in medicine will be announced Monday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Despair over future fuels political anxiety for college students on the cusp of adulthood
item.description: Their anxiety is fueling a restlessness with a national political system that they worry is no longer capable of improving their lives or no longer interested in helping.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: The misperception that keeps bystanders from intervening and how to short‑circuit it
item.description: People may accept bad behavior — even sexual assault — when they overestimate how acceptable their peers think it is. But there are ways to undermine this thinking and make intervention more likely.

item.title: NPR: Trump names national intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new AI czar
item.description: Trump said Clayton will lead the White House's new "Super Intelligence Force," which will coordinate government engagement with artificial intelligence.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Search ongoing for missing medical flight from Bermuda to Boston as crews plan to scour ocean floor
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration contacted the Coast Guard at 2 a.m. Saturday that it had lost contact with the Gulfstream G100 carrying four Canadians and two Bermudian nationals over the Atlantic Ocean.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Bosnia votes as pro-Russian politician looms large and ethnic tensions simmer
item.description: Around 3.4 million voters are choosing the three members of the country's multi-ethnic presidency, lawmakers for the national Parliament and heads of institutions for the country's two entities.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump names national intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new federal AI task force
item.description: The announcement comes after Trump hosted top executives of AI companies at the White House last week and said they had signed a voluntary accord that would effectively self-police the development of the technology.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP report: UAE had shared details about FlyDubai flight with Israel, including pilots' names and nationalities
item.description: With the investigation underway, preliminary details about the incident have highlighted several major security lapses.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Christa Pike's lawyer says she has not regained consciousness since her failed Tennessee execution
item.description: Little has been released about Pike's condition since Wednesday night's execution attempt. She has since remained hospitalized under guard as doctors try to get the massive dose of the barbiturate pentobarbital out of her system.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brazil's presidential vote pits Trump ally against incumbent Lula
item.description: Bolsonaro is the son of far-right former President Jair Bolsonaro and an ally of U.S. President Donald Trump. Lula is running in his seventh presidential election and has strengthened Brazil's ties with Beijing.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Cornell president calls alleged gang rape 'deeply disturbing,' pledges greater transparency
item.description: "My heart aches when I think of what she experienced," Kotlikoff said. "It raises heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanization and aspects of party culture, alcohol and drug use."

item.title: NPR: Failed 'torturous' execution attempt on Christa Pike reignites death penalty debate
item.description: The botched execution in Tennessee of Christa Pike, who survived despite being subject to two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday, has reignited furious debate about the death penalty in the U.S.

item.title: NPR: Midterm voting is underway. Some voters are relying on AI to make a decision
item.description: Voters are already voting in the midterms. This year, some voters are trying something new to get ready for the election: asking AI to help research their ballot and even decide who to vote for.

item.title: NPR: Politics chat: Midterm polls, Senate races, Trump in Texas
item.description: As polls come out with increasing frequency closer to the midterm election, how much credence should voters give them? Meanwhile, President Trump continues campaigning for GOP candidates.

item.title: NPR: Latter-day Saints women turn away from scandal-plagued Republican candidate in Arizona
item.description: Arizona Republican candidate for Congress Mark Lamb has been accused of sexual misconduct while sheriff. His controversy is turning many voters away as Democrats see an opportunity in the red seat.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A $28 billion hemp THC industry is fighting to save itself from a looming federal ban
item.description: America's multibillion-dollar market for impairing hemp products faces potential elimination after Congress voted to close a loophole in federal law that has allowed it to flourish.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump rallies in Ohio to boost Jon Husted in a tight Senate race against Sherrod Brown
item.description: Saturday's rally is just outside Dayton, Ohio, where he'll stump for key candidates in competitive races for the House, Senate and the governor's mansion in Columbus.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Inside the study for a remedy to fight Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak
item.description: The drug is targeted at Bundibugyo virus, which is responsible for the fast-moving outbreak and is without an approved vaccine or treatment. The trial began in July and is one of several studies launched to find some protection and another way of at least slowing the outbreak.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What to know about the Kelvin wave raising the sea level along the West Coast
item.description: Kelvin waves are not like tsunamis, and they don't curl over and crash on the beach. A better image is water sloshing in the bathtub or a swimming pool during an earthquake. In the ocean, they are bulges of water that lift the sea level as they move along the coast.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Trump urges calls to Arkansas Sen. Tom Cotton in push for permanent daylight saving time
item.description: "For some reason, Tom is stopping the Bill and, in the Senate, it's very easy to do, it only takes one!" Trump wrote on social media, noting that passing the bill would give professional golfers more time on the greens.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Prosecutor says 2 Iranian men scouted a UK synagogue for a chlorine bomb plot
item.description: The Heaton Park synagogue was the site of an attack on Yom Kippur, the holiest day of the Jewish calendar, on Oct. 2, 2025, when Jihad Al-Shamie crashed his car into the gates and then began a knife attack.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A gut punch in Ohio: Nearly 1,400 laid off at truck factory just days before Trump rally
item.description: This year's election is a test for the working-class coalition that lifted Trump into the White House and gave majorities to Republicans in the House and Senate.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Woman told Cornell investigators she 'felt like bait' during alleged gang rape
item.description: While heavily redacted, the records offer a fuller but sometimes conflicting timeline of events and a glimpse at how the men responded to the allegations. Some disputed the woman's account and said they weren't involved in any assault.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Governor says Tennessee's prisons chief is resigning after failed execution of Christa Pike
item.description: Frank Strada said in a statement that stepping aside "is in the best interests" of the state as an independent review is carried out to determine why Pike's execution failed Wednesday.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Dual UK-Iranian national released on bail over suspected plot against U.S.-run military base
item.description: The 25-year-old man was arrested Thursday in London on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts close to the RAF Fairford air base, which has been used by American bombers to strike Iran. He was the sixth person taken into custody and then released on bail as detectives investigate the incident.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP report: Axe-wielding FlyDubai co-pilot had been flagged over extremism concerns
item.description: The new details raised questions about how thoroughly FlyDubai vets potential employees, and how the co-pilot's presence on a flight filled with Israeli passengers got past Israel's strict security protocols.

item.title: NPR: Week in Politics: Inflation pressure; war in Iran and effect on midterm elections
item.description: We look at how some concerning economic indicators as well as the ongoing war in Iran might affect the midterm elections.

item.title: NPR: How high-profile scandals are shaping key contests ahead of the midterms
item.description: Scandals could be shaping several races in the midterm elections, particularly in places where even small margins can change the outcome.

item.title: NPR: California voters to decide on controversial one-time tax on billionaires
item.description: California voters will decide whether the state will charge a one-time tax on billionaires. The idea that has split Democrats and labor unions.

item.title: NPR: En esta ciudad de Pensilvania, los dos partidos políticos buscan el voto latino
item.description: Los republicanos lograron avances con los latinos en el último ciclo electoral, pero la economía y la frustración por la política migratoria de Donald Trump han corroído ese apoyo.

item.title: NPR: The Supreme Court faces another term jam-packed with controversy
item.description: The Supreme Court term opens on Monday with big test cases on religion, guns and climate change. Plus, the emergency docket keeps popping.

item.title: NPR: Trade tensions mean fewer Canadians flocking to South Florida
item.description: This South Florida community is typically a refuge for Canadians fleeing cold weather, but trade tensions between the United States and Canada mean fewer are coming.

item.title: NPR: Along U.S. Route 1, Maine voters worry about heating oil, gas and Canadian tariffs
item.description: Home to both Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic candidate Troy Jackson, Maine's senate race has put rural Aroostook County in the spotlight.

item.title: NPR: COMIC: How the census gives your state power (and what Trump wants to change)
item.description: The census is used to determine how much say your state has in Congress and the Electoral College. President Trump failed to alter it during his first term, but he's trying again ahead of 2030.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: FBI gives employees a classified 'Patel Report' about times the agency 'fell short'
item.description: The document's existence is in keeping with Director Kash Patel's vocal criticism of the leaders who preceded him

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Could the International Space Station win a Nobel Peace Prize? Here's what to know
item.description: Not-so-outlandish, prognosticators say: The Nobel Peace Prize this year could go galactic, with an award to the International Space Station.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge halts border wall construction in Texas' Big Bend region for now
item.description: A federal court in Texas on Friday issued a ruling temporarily blocking the Trump administration from building a border wall and other infrastructure across the state's Big Bend region, in a victory for opponents who have pushed back against what has long been a key campaign promise by President Donald Trump.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What a hiring slowdown signals about the state of the U.S. economy
item.description: U.S. hiring slowed in September as employers added just 29,000 jobs. The disappointing jobs report has wide-reaching implications for consumer prices and interest rates, and it comes a month before Americans head to the polls for midterm elections. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Beth Hammack, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: New York AG appointed as special prosecutor in Cornell rape case
item.description: In our news wrap Friday, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed the state Attorney General Letitia James as a special prosecutor to take over the Cornell University rape case, the U.S. is sending an additional aircraft carrier to the Middle East as President Trump weighs further action against Iran and this year's Kennedy Center Honors will take place at Washington, D.C.'s Capital One Arena.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Who's spending big, and where, in most expensive election cycle ever
item.description: Spending for this year's midterms is accelerating as we get closer to Election Day. Political correspondent Lisa Desjardins makes sense of the billions spent to influence who controls Congress next year.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A look at how overseas ballots are verified and counted in the midterms
item.description: Defense Secretary Hegseth directed military commanders to have a one-day "stand down" this month so service members have time to vote in the midterms. In King County, Washington, ballots are already being processed from service members and Americans living abroad. Some arrive by mail. Some by email. Liz Landers takes a look at how those ballots are verified and counted and how secure they are.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Brooks and Atkins Stohr on GOP vulnerabilities in the midterms
item.description: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Kimberly Atkins Stohr of The Boston Globe join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including President Trump hitting the campaign trail in a string of reliably Republican states, GOP vulnerabilities heading into the midterms and the administration's strategy on artificial intelligence.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: How the West is preparing for a drier future as water supplies hit lows
item.description: Mandatory cuts from the federal government on water from the Colorado River will soon take effect in Arizona, Nevada, and California. Now, some water managers in the region are spending billions to prepare for a drier future. Special correspondent Ben Tracy with Climate Central reports for our series, Tipping Point.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Martina Navratilova on Chris Evert, their rivalry and beating cancer
item.description: Martina Navratilova was a high-profile force on the tennis court in the 1970s and 80s with 59 Grand Slam titles. She has remained a big presence in the tennis world, commentating and mentoring, and is using her platform to weigh in on issues off the court as well. Amna Nawaz sat down with Navratilova for our culture of sport coverage, part of our CANVAS series.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Utah's U.S. House candidates Maloy, Udell meet for midterm debate
item.description: Utah's Republican Rep. Celeste Maloy will face off in a debate Friday against Democratic candidate Kent Udell as voters consider whom to send to the U.S. House.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Supreme Court ready to tackle climate, immigration and gun rights. Here are 5 cases to watch
item.description: When the U.S. Supreme Court returns Monday, the justices will kick off a new term featuring cases on climate change, gun rights, immigration and religious liberty.

item.title: NPR: As Trump's proposed arch looms over D.C., protesters pin their hopes on the midterms
item.description: Democratic lawmakers, veterans and concerned citizens gathered in Memorial Circle to protest the arch Trump wants to build there. Their hopes lie primarily in a lawsuit and next month's midterms.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Christa Pike on a ventilator and unconscious after failed Tennessee execution, attorneys say
item.description: The stunning failure in Tennessee's execution chamber on Wednesday has left both sides of the death penalty debate demanding answers. Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee has ordered an independent review.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Former GOP Rep. David Rivera sentenced to 10 years for secret Venezuela lobbying
item.description: David Rivera has been jailed since jurors found him guilty in May on all counts, including failing to register as a foreign agent and conspiracy to commit money laundering as part of his work for former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro's government.

item.title: NPR: Pro-Trump Influencer Benny Johnson is being sued for defamation by ICE protesters
item.description: The lawsuit says the prominent conservative podcaster falsely claimed the protesters were assaulting ICE officers during demonstrations at an ICE facility in Illinois last year.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Many states have backup execution plans, but failures still happen
item.description: Twenty-seven states have capital punishment, and they vary widely in how they administer the death penalty and just how much of that lethal process they keep hidden from public view, according to the nonprofit Death Penalty Information Center.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New ICE guidance bans high-speed car chases and sets tighter rules for traffic stops, memo shows
item.description: The new guidance comes after ICE-initiated vehicle stops have repeatedly escalated when drivers have refused to cooperate or tried to flee. ICE agents have fired their guns during more than a dozen such encounters since last year, killing at least four people and wounding several others.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Federal prosecutors charge shop clerk and son with selling kratom thought to be tied to Ole Miss death
item.description: The U.S. attorney's office in Mississippi said authorities established a link between the kratom derivative found at the scene of the student's death and a local vape, tobacco and beer store.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Kennedy Center Honors to be held at Capital One Arena amid fight over adding Trump's name
item.description: The 49th annual awards are set to take place at Washington's downtown arena, a Kennedy Center spokesperson said Friday. Few other details were immediately available, and an explanation for the change wasn't given.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Pilot stabbing further unsettles region shaken by U.S.-Iran war
item.description: The UAE has canceled all flights to Israel, complicating travel for hundreds of passengers who fly between the countries on a typical day.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Hegseth creates a Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs that reports directly to him
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has infused his evangelical Christianity into his leadership of the Pentagon, hosting Christian worship services for employees and often speaking of the United States as a Christian nation.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: AP report: Senate Republicans move cash from North Carolina to Kansas as battle for majority shifts
item.description: The moves offer a stark sign of how dramatically the Senate map has shifted just a month before midterm elections that will determine control of Congress.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Trump holds rally in Alabama as he tries to boost midterm enthusiasm
item.description: Republicans have expressed growing pessimism about their chances in the election, which will determine control of Congress, as the president has repeatedly dismissed concerns about high costs and gas prices as his unpopular war in Iran drags on.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: G7 nations agree to release 100 million barrels of oil, including diesel
item.description: President Donald Trump and his Republican Party face pressure to address surging prices ahead of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, and Trump announced the action Friday on social media.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: LIVE MAP: Track the path of Hurricane Rachel
item.description: Hurricane Rachel has been upgraded to a Category 3 storm off Mexico's Pacific coast as northern Mexico and parts of the U.S. Southwest were reeling from flooding and damage from the remnants of Hurricane Polo earlier this week.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Disappointing 29,000 jobs added in September as unemployment ticks up
item.description: Friday's jobs report is the last one that will come out before the Nov. 3 elections that will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republicans maintain full control of Congress.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: WATCH LIVE: Cornell sexual assault investigation update with Gov. Hochul, NY Attorney General James
item.description: Gov. Kathy Hochul announced Thursday she appointed the office of Attorney General Letitia James as the special prosecutor to oversee the investigation, saying she had lost faith in the local district attorney's ability to handle the case.

item.title: NPR: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
item.description: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.

item.title: NPR: Failed 'torturous' execution attempt on Christa Pike reignites death penalty debate
item.description: The botched execution in Tennessee of Christa Pike – who survived despite being subject to two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday – has reignited furious debate about the death penalty in the U.S.

item.title: NPR: The U.S. Senate is up for grabs. Can this Ohio Democrat win back working class votes?
item.description: After 32 years in Congress, Ohio's Sherrod Brown lost his Senate seat in 2024 as many working class voters turned out for Trump. Now Brown is counting on union voters to send him back to Washington.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A fact-checked guide to Trump's talking points and falsehoods at midterm rallies
item.description: President Donald Trump is hitting the campaign trail to support Republican candidates in toss-up races that will determine which party controls Congress for the final two years of his presidency. Here's a list of more than two dozen go-to Trump statements and how they square for accuracy.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Judge denies motion asking for Lindsay Clancy to be found not guilty due to lack of evidence
item.description: The judge in the Lindsay Clancy murder case on Thursday refused to declare her not guilty, turning down a defense motion that had argued there wasn't enough evidence to prove she was responsible for killing her three children.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: What we know about Tennessee's botched execution of Christa Pike
item.description: Tennessee officials failed to carry out the lethal injection of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday. Her attorneys say she is alive and in critical condition after being given two separate doses of pentobarbital meant to kill her. Pike was sentenced to death for the gruesome murder of her classmate in 1995. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Deborah Denno, a professor at Fordham School of Law.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Investigators search for motive after alleged attack by FlyDubai co-pilot
item.description: Investigators across the Middle East are hunting for answers after a co-pilot stabbed his captain and allegedly attempted to crash a FlyDubai aircraft bound for Israel. President Trump claimed the attack could be linked to Iran, but did not provide evidence. Geoff Bennett discussed what we do and don't know with Juliette Kayyem, a former assistant secretary at the Department of Homeland Security.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: Student protests grip France as Prime Minister Lecornu calls crisis meeting
item.description: The demonstrations erupted in Paris-region schools last week and have snowballed, with police making hundreds of arrests in clashes with the young protesters.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: News Wrap: Supreme Court to review mandatory detention policy for migrants
item.description: In our news wrap Thursday, the Supreme Court agreed to review the Trump administration's mandatory detention policy for migrants, UK police arrested a British-Iranian citizen on suspicion of planning a terror attack following a security incident at an air base and a Russian drone slammed into a school in Kyiv as the capital endured yet another day of aerial attacks.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: New details intensify scrutiny of Cornell's handling of gang rape allegations
item.description: There are new revelations about how authorities handled an alleged gang rape at Cornell University in 2024. New reporting out today finds Cornell police left out key information in a statement given to local law enforcement. That includes Jane Doe's statement, "I can say with 100 percent confidence I was raped." Amna Nawaz discussed more with Sharon Otterman of The New York Times.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: A look at Hegseth's attempts to reshape the Pentagon
item.description: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth says he is fundamentally reshaping the culture of the U.S. military. He's removing senior officers, dismantling diversity initiatives and putting a new emphasis on religious faith and what he calls a "warrior ethos." Beyond the cultural changes, Hegseth is accelerating autonomous weapons and other emerging technologies. Geoff Bennett discussed more with Peter Feaver.

item.title: PBS NewsHour: 'Valley of Death' reveals how tech companies are replacing traditional defense contractors
item.description: Efforts to reshape the military include modernizing the technology soldiers will use on the battlefield and the further integration of artificial intelligence. Some of the biggest names in Silicon Valley are working with the Pentagon and cashing in. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Sharon Weinberger, author of "Valley of Death: How Big Tech Is Fueling the Future of War."

item.title: PBS NewsHour: On the ground with UN peacekeepers as Lebanon-Israel mission nears its end
item.description: After 48 years, the United Nations peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon is nearing the end of its mandate. Its planned withdrawal comes at a time when the Israeli military occupies around 6% of Lebanese territory. Special Correspondent Simona Foltyn and videographer Adrian Hartrick gained rare access with the peacekeepers, traveling south of Israel's "yellow line."
